LESSON: LINEAR MOTION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CORE MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements and Geometry
Topic 2.9: Linear Motion
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Linear Motion, part of Measurements and Geometry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 CORE MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use displacement- time graphs in real life? 2. How do we use velocity-time graphs?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. demonstrate motion by moving an object from a point to another for a specified distance and direction and state the meaning of the terms distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or be assisted by peers/learner 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. demonstrate motion by moving an object from a point to another for a specified distance and direction and state the meaning of the terms distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or be assisted by peers/learner 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Linear Motion together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses different displacement-time graphs.

● Self-Efficacy: as the learner participates in a race of a specified distance, record time taken by a learner and work

out the velocity and acceleration.

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: as the learner observes two bodies in motion such as cars when overtaking

or moving in opposite directions and works out the relative speed of the two bodies in motion.

64

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner uses objects in motion such as thrown objects and many others to explain distance,

displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration.

● Integrity: as the learner participates in a race of a specified distance, records time taken by each learner and

accurately works out the velocity and acceleration of different learners.

● Unity: as the learner participates and collaborates in a race to record time taken by each learner and work out the

velocity and acceleration of different learners.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Learner Support Programmes-Sports and Games: as the learner participates in a race of a specified distance,

records time taken by each learner and works out the velocity and acceleration.

● Socio-Economic and Environmental Issues-Safety and Security: as the learner observes the two bodies in motion

such as cars when overtaking or moving in opposite directions and works out the relative speed of these two

bodies in motion.

● Road safety: as the learner observes two vehicles when one is overtaking, discusses and works out the relative

speed of the two vehicles. Also discusses the dangers of careless overtaking.

Suggested Learning Resources

Geometrical instruments such as rulers with enhanced grip, metre rule with handle, mathematical tables, charts on

multiplication tables/ motion-time graphs, drawing/ manila/ graph papers, scissors with enhanced grip, solid objects,

multipurpose communication boards on solid objects, white boards, slant boards, book holders, head pointers, page

turners, pen/pencil holders, adapted scientific calculators/ projectors, positioning devices such as special seats with straps,

adapted digital devices such as adapted computers with larger screens
